attempts.raw: TEXT Conversation Engine owns messages and lineage, managing the flow and history of interactions. Context Engine selects relevant references and budgets their use, focusing on context relevance and resource limits. Application Orchestrator coordinates both engines, ensuring clear interfaces and communication protocols. To decouple them: define explicit APIs for message handling (Conversation Engine) and context selection (Context Engine); use asynchronous messaging or event-driven patterns for interaction; isolate state management within each engine; apply dependency inversion so Orchestrator depends on abstractions, not implementations; and enforce clear responsibility boundaries to minimize direct dependencies and allow independent evolution.

Numeric + - * /, == > <, condition ? yes : no, arrays, objects, named references, @Sum(numbers), @Sort(rows,"score","desc") are allowed. No unary minus, concatenation, member access, map, interpolation or inline nested components. Produce complete root and definitions.

attempts.raw: TEXT To decouple a Conversation Engine (handling messages and lineage), a Context Engine (selecting and budgeting references), and an Application Orchestrator (coordinating them), follow these principles: 1) Define clear, minimal APIs for each engine to expose their core functions without leaking internal details. 2) Use asynchronous communication or event-driven messaging between components to avoid tight coupling and blocking calls. 3) Keep state management isolated within each engine to prevent shared mutable state. 4) The Application Orchestrator should depend on abstractions (interfaces) of the engines, enabling swapping or independent updates. 5) Enforce single responsibility per engine: Conversation Engine manages dialogue flow and history; Context Engine manages reference selection and resource budgeting; Orchestrator manages workflow and coordination logic. This separation allows independent development, testing, and scaling of each component.
